clue.text: I produce powerful retro Affleck vehicle that is (cutting speed) still quite hard to see

indicators.note: the long run of letters cuts into the abbreviation for speed, splitting it

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, is the usual abbreviation for a speed
to crop is to yield or produce a harvest
hot as in strong or powerful, like a hot favourite or hot curry

indicators.note: retro means going backwards, so the film title is read in reverse

parts.note: Argo is a film directed by and starring Ben Affleck, a star vehicle

explanation.surface: A boastful film producer brags about his mighty retro Affleck movie, oddly described as barely visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' reverses the film title and 'cutting' puts the long run inside the speed abbreviation. 'Still' is a noun here, a still photograph, and 'that is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, and one so reduced in size that it needs magnifying is a tiny image indeed.

clue.text: Boarding pass is, for now

definitions.meaning: a boarding pass is the document a traveller carries in order to be allowed on the plane: read cryptically, it is what you need to get going on board
for the time being, as a temporary measure

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: a boarding pass is literally a thing for being allowed to go on (board).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something sufficient for the present, temporarily, until something better arrives.

clue.text: See 11
Constipated chap to eat Italian special up

indicators.note: the chap swallows the reversed letters, so they go inside him

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A bunged-up man is told to eat an Italian speciality to get things moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses IT and S into STI, which COVE is 'to eat', giving CO-STI-VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Costive is a dated, rather formal adjective for suffering from constipation; it also means sluggish or slow.

clue.text: See 12
Get organised, or be spontaneous on one

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are told to get themselves into order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to someone: either plan things properly or just act on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes all of 'or be spontaneous', fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried about one's person is kept on the body, in a pocket or bag, so it is literally with you.

clue.text: Ring up worried customer, a little overdrawn, about cash supply — the problem?

definitions.text: Ring up worried customer, a little overdrawn, about cash supply — the problem?

indicators.note: about means around: the rearranged phone phrase goes round the twisted money word
worried in the sense of agitated or troubled, so the letters of the phone phrase are shaken into a new order
read as an adverb, supply means in a supple, bendy way, so the money word is twisted

parts.note: a customer who is overdrawn by a penny owes P: P (penny) plus OWER, one who owes

explanation.surface: A bank rings up an anxious customer who is slightly in the red about the cash they have available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not a noun but the adverb of supple, the anagram signal for CASH; that sits 'about'-wise inside the 'worried' RING UP. The whole clue also describes the overdrawn customer's difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying power is the amount of goods one's money can obtain, exactly what an overdrawn bank customer lacks.

clue.text: King Louis bursting to play with vigour!

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: bursting means breaking apart, so the letters of the king's name are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A French king bursts out, urging someone to play energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis' looks like a French king and 'King' like a title for him, but King is R (Rex) and the name is merely letters for 'bursting'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Italian musical direction telling a performer to play resolutely, boldly and with firmness.

clue.text: Originally, Alan Rusbridger beat the Guardian's retreat

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: the Guardian's own newspaper speaking of itself would say our

explanation.surface: The newspaper's former editor Alan Rusbridger beats a retreat from the Guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is in the Guardian, so the paper's own possessive is OUR. Alan Rusbridger was a long-serving Guardian editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower or shady garden shelter is a secluded place to withdraw to, a retreat.

clue.text: Make available for emptying liquidised fruit over, but run out

indicators.note: emptying the little word removes its middle, leaving only its first and last letters
out means the letter for run is removed
over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: fruit blended to a smooth pulp is purée
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Instructions for clearing a blender: empty the puréed fruit, but you have run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptying' leaves FR from 'for'; 'over' turns PUREE into EERUP and 'out' drops R (run), leaving EEUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To release something from a commitment so that it can be used elsewhere is to make it available.

clue.text: Lesson once taught in pool to would-be paddler about superior speed?

definitions.text: Lesson once taught in pool to would-be paddler about superior speed?

parts.words: Lesson once taught in pool to would-be paddler about superior speed?
parts.note: the pool is a typing pool, where trainee typists (who paddle at keys) practised a sentence using every letter, and that sentence is a tale of one animal outpacing another

explanation.surface: It sounds like a swimming lesson in a pool for a child learning to paddle, about going faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimming pool is really a typing pool: offices once trained typists on a pangram, a sentence containing all 26 letters, which happens to be about a nimble animal leaping a sluggish one.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous pangram was the standard practice sentence for typists, since it exercises every key on the keyboard.

clue.text: Modern girlfriend's choice!

definitions.meaning: current, fashionable, in line with the latest developments
if the girlfriend is one's ..., a decision that is hers is left to the ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a choice left to your date is 'up to (the) date'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something current or fashionable is in step with the latest ideas, the opposite of old-fashioned.

clue.text: A short service for Ratty in love with Toad

indicators.note: ratty means irritable and out of sorts, so the letters are disturbed; Ratty is also the Water Rat of The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A wedding scene from The Wind in the Willows: a brief ceremony for Ratty, who has fallen for Toad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratty' looks like the character, but it is the anagram signal applied to IN LOVE plus TOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotional is a brief act of religious worship or prayer, often held outside the main church services.

clue.text: See 11
Dramatically, novice then losing the plot

indicators.note: dramatically suggests something changed in a striking way, so the letters are rearranged
losing means the three-letter word is taken away from the four-letter word, leaving just its last letter

explanation.surface: An inexperienced actor on stage suddenly forgets what is happening in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes THE from THEN, leaving N; 'Dramatically' rearranges NOVICE plus N. 'The plot' wants to be a story's plot, but 'plot' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire or scheme together secretly, especially to allow wrongdoing, is to plot.

clue.text: Make it with iniquity?

parts.note: to make it with someone is slang for to have sex with them, to bed them
iniquity is wickedness, evil

explanation.surface: It reads like a question about sleeping with wickedness itself.
explanation.walkthrough: To bed (have sex with) evil is, playfully, to fill something with devilry, to bewitch or plague it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to torment or plague, originally to possess as if by a demon, which is wickedness getting into things.

clue.text: Leaving shortly, splitting bill to share the planet

indicators.note: the shortened word splits the bill, going inside it

parts.note: the bill is the cost to be paid

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an exit is a departure, a leaving

explanation.surface: Diners leaving soon split the bill, while also living together on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' docks the last letter of the word for leaving, and 'splitting' sends it inside the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To live alongside one another in peace, as different species or nations do on Earth, is to share the world.

clue.text: I agree men will get blown away after horologer's awful windiness

indicators.note: after means the single remaining letter comes at the end
awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the clockmaker's name supplies the letters, the 's being the possessive link

indicators.note: blown away means the three letters are removed from the word of agreement

parts.note: amen, said at the end of a prayer, means so be it, I agree
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that men will be put off by a clockmaker's dreadful flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown away' removes the men from the word of agreement, leaving A, which goes 'after' the 'awful' scramble. 'Windiness' is long-windedness, not wind.
explanation.definitionFit: It is excessive talkativeness, verbal diarrhoea, and windiness means wordy, long-winded speech.

clue.text: See 21
See 11
Thus spread leaf and elements of plug?

definitions.text: Thus spread leaf and elements of plug?

indicators.note: spread means the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A magazine advertisement (a plug) printed across a whole leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges LEAF and PLUG; the whole clue describes an advert that fills a page, a full-page spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is an advertisement, and one taking up a whole leaf of a magazine is a page-filling spread.

clue.text: Adam's first to broach concern over herbal plant

indicators.note: broach means to pierce, so the letter pierces the reversed word
over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: worry means anxiety, concern

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Adam is the first to raise a concern over a herbal plant, as in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns WORRY into YRROW, and A goes 'to broach' it after the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Achillea millefolium, a feathery-leaved wild plant long used in herbal remedies.

clue.text: How's your father gaining admission to South China lazaretto?

indicators.note: the slang word for sex is admitted inside the pair of letters

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a pal
how's your father is British slang for sex, and so is it

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a parent being admitted to a quarantine hospital in southern China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is a jokey British euphemism for sex, as is 'it'; china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate. 'Gaining admission to' puts the sex word inside the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazaretto is an old hospital for infectious diseases such as leprosy; a spital is an archaic word for the same kind of hospital.

clue.text: This break the making of Loadsamoney?

definitions.text: This break the making of Loadsamoney?

parts.words: This break the making of Loadsamoney?
parts.note: Loadsamoney, Harry Enfield's cash-flashing comic character, means pots of money: the first four letters read backwards over themselves give pots, the making of loadsa money

explanation.walkthrough: Loadsamoney was a 1980s British comedy character who waved wads of cash. Read the first half backwards and you get POTS, as in pots of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief halt on a journey, especially an overnight stay between flights, is a break in travel.
